frictions.title: Focus escapes Important Event Info modal into background page content
frictions.description: Opening the 'Important Event Info' modal overlay allows VoiceOver focus to escape into background page elements when navigating past modal controls, forcing the user to backtrack to relocate the dialog content (WCAG 2.4.3).

interventions.description: Contain focus within the Important Event Info modal dialog while active.

After activating the 'Important Info' button, the 'Important Event Info' overlay opened, but sequential VoiceOver navigation (VO-Right) past the modal's close button moved into background page layout groups instead of remaining within the dialog. The user had to issue repeated VO-Left commands to return to the modal content. Because the underlying page content is not isolated while the overlay is active, screen reader users can silently leave the dialog, lose their reading position, and cannot reliably tell which content belongs to the overlay versus the obscured page behind it.
interventions.mitigation: Scope the overlay so assistive technology only exposes dialog content while it is open: give the modal container an appropriate dialog role with aria-modal="true", and/or apply inert (or aria-hidden) to the background page containers while the overlay is displayed. Keep keyboard tab cycling constrained to the interactive elements inside the overlay, move focus into the dialog on open, and return focus to the invoking 'Important Info' button on close. Verify with VoiceOver that VO-Right/VO-Left traversal past the first and last dialog controls stays inside the overlay.

blind.description: The interactive seat map is an SVG of bare <circle class="seat"> elements with no role, accessible name, or focusability (the .map__zoomer wrapper is tabindex="-1"), so screen-reader users cannot perceive or select individual seats.

Seat status in the map is conveyed only through CSS classes/colors (e.g. "seat is-available is-filtered") with no text or programmatic equivalent, so availability and price tiers are unavailable non-visually.

The ticket list is marked up as role="menu" with role="menuitem" rows whose prices are non-interactive <span> elements (e.g. id="quickpick-buy-button-qp-0" with tabindex="-1"), so listings are announced as an application menu rather than selectable ticket buttons.

Static informational text is injected into that menu as a disabled menuitem (
  • We’re All In: Prices include fees…
    • ), polluting the menu semantics and confusing arrow-key navigation.

The whole ticket-selection region (#edp-main-ismqp with the filters, quick-picks list and map) does not appear in the exposed accessibility tree, which contains only the header, side menu and calendar, leaving screen-reader users with no path to buy tickets.

Every calendar date button carries aria-hidden="true" while its container is a focusable div with role="menu" tabindex="0", producing a focusable element with no announced content and hiding the event date grid from assistive technology.

The calendar month label <h2 id="calendar-current-month" aria-live="assertive" aria-hidden="true"> combines a live region with aria-hidden, so month changes are never announced, and the month grid uses role="tablist" over plain date buttons that are not tabs.

The price filter inputs use the invalid role="text" and embed their current value in the label (aria-label="Minimum price $53" / "Maximum price $87"), so the name becomes stale and the control's role is unsupported.
The side-menu search field (input#search-full-input) is exposed with no accessible name in the accessibility tree despite the associated <label>, so its purpose is unclear when focused.

The entire side navigation is wrapped in <nav class="menu" aria-live="polite"> with no aria-label, so opening it can dump the whole menu (search, help links, app badges, legal copy) into the speech queue as one announcement.
Menu section titles use <div role="heading"> ("We're Here to Help", "Friends & Partners", "Download Our Apps") without aria-level, leaving the heading hierarchy undefined.
The event title is duplicated as two separate <h1> elements (header and hero block), so screen-reader users hear the same top-level heading twice and cannot rely on heading structure.

The "Important Info" disclosure button (accessibility/elevator notice) exposes only the visually truncated text ending in "..." and provides no aria-expanded state, so the full venue accessibility information and the control's state are not conveyed.
The sort controls are <span role="tab"> elements with no aria-controls and the associated role="tabpanel" has no accessible name, breaking the tab/panel relationship for screen readers.

Dynamic status areas such as the empty <div class="notification-popup__message"> and the ticket-bag subtotal/quantity ($0.00, 0 Tickets) are not live regions, so updates after filtering or selecting tickets are not announced.

low_vision.description: The viewport meta tag sets maximum-scale=1.0 and user-scalable=no, preventing pinch-zoom magnification of the ticket list, prices and seat map on touch devices.

Available versus unavailable seats in the SVG map are differentiated only by fill color (is-available / plain .seat classes) with no shape, label or pattern cue, which is unreliable for users with low vision or color deficiency.
Individual seat targets are 40-unit-radius circles inside a 10240×7680 viewBox rendered into a small map container, producing extremely small click/tap targets that are hard to hit when magnified.

The venue accessibility notice is visually truncated with an ellipsis in a fixed-height button ("…We encourage patrons ..." plus a "more" link), so at increased text size or zoom essential information is clipped rather than reflowed.
Each listing relies on a fixed 85×72px raster minimap image (mapsapi.tmol.io …&w=85) to show seat location, which pixelates and cannot be enlarged when the page is magnified.

frictions.title: Important Event Info modal content unannounced during VoiceOver navigation
frictions.description: Activating the 'Important Info' disclosure control opens the 'Important Event Info' modal, but VoiceOver navigation skips the venue accessibility body text, cycling only between the heading, close button, and unannounced group containers.

interventions.description: Activating the 'Important Info' disclosure control opens the 'Important Event Info' modal dialog, but the paragraph text containing the venue accessibility details (e.g. elevator information) is never reached by the VoiceOver cursor. Across more than 25 VO navigation keypresses, speech output cycled only between the level 2 heading, the close button, and container groups that were announced without any name or meaningful role. The consequence is that a screen reader user cannot read the accessibility notice at all, so the information needed to decide whether the venue can accommodate them is effectively unavailable, even though it is visually present in the dialog.
interventions.mitigation: Ensure the dialog's body content is exposed in the accessibility tree and reachable by the screen reader cursor. Concretely: verify that the dialog container uses role="dialog" with aria-modal="true" and an accessible name via aria-labelledby pointing to the visible heading, and that the descriptive paragraph is a real text node inside the dialog rather than hidden from AT (check for aria-hidden="true", role="presentation", inert, display/visibility hiding, or focus/AT scoping applied to the wrong subtree). Remove any generic wrapper elements that add unnamed groups to the traversal without semantic value, or give them appropriate roles/labels. After the fix, validate with VoiceOver that Control-Option arrow navigation from the heading reaches the full notice text, and consider associating the body copy with the dialog via aria-describedby so it is announced when focus enters.

items.pathway_description: Tab reveals the skip link; activation does nothing and the user must Tab through the whole navigation.

frictions.description: The 'Skip to main content' link is announced with the wrong role and its target anchor is missing or unfocusable, so activating it leaves focus at the top of the page.

items.description: Inject the missing focusable main-content target and correct the skip link's semantics so activation moves focus into the main content.

frictions.title: Broken skip link target prevents bypassing header content
frictions.description: The 'Skip to main content' link references '#main-content', but no element on the page possesses that ID. Activating the link fails to shift focus to the main content area, resulting in repeated unproductive activations.

interventions.description: Fix the 'Skip to main content' link by attaching the target ID 'main-content' to the primary page container.

The homepage exposes a 'Skip to main content' link whose href references the fragment '#main-content', but the DOM contains no element with id='main-content'. When the user activated the link with VoiceOver (VO-Space), focus did not move to the main content region; it remained at the top of the page. This was observed across two distinct episodes, with the user re-triggering the link more than ten times before abandoning the attempt. Consequently, screen reader and keyboard users have no working mechanism to bypass the repeated header and site navigation block and must traverse the entire header on every page visit.
interventions.mitigation: Make the skip link's target resolvable and focusable: assign id="main-content" to the element that actually wraps the primary page content (matching the existing href value) and give that container tabindex="-1" so browsers can place programmatic focus on it. Verify after the change that activating the link moves both the DOM focus and the VoiceOver cursor into the main content container rather than leaving them at the top of the document. Where the fragment target cannot be added to the intended container, update the link's href to point at an existing focusable landmark instead, and add an automated check that every in-page fragment link resolves to a real element ID to prevent regressions.

The full primary menu is duplicated in the DOM (ul#superfish-main-accordion and ul#superfish-main contain the same Services/About/Documents/News/Jobs links), so screen-reader users hear every navigation link twice.

items.pathway_description: Linear VO navigation skips the grid entirely; the user never learns the timetable exists.

frictions.description: The availability timetable is a mouse-only grid of positioned divs with no focusability, grid semantics, or keyboard selection, so VoiceOver cannot enter it or select slots.

items.description: Inject grid, row, and gridcell semantics with labels, selection state, roving focus, arrow-key navigation, and Space/Enter activation onto the timetable.

frictions.title: When2Meet availability grid slots lack ARIA semantics and focusability
frictions.description: Interactive time slot cells in the scheduling grid are unsemantic div elements lacking ARIA roles, tabindex, and accessible names. VoiceOver and keyboard navigation skip all slots, leaving only static time labels exposed, preventing nonvisual users from marking availability.

interventions.description: Expose availability grid slots as operable controls with accessible date and time names and keyboard support.

The interactive time slot cells in the availability grid are implemented as generic div elements that carry no ARIA role, no accessible name, and no tabindex, and are activated only through pointer/mouse handlers. As observed, Tab and Shift+Tab skipped the entire grid (focus jumped from timezone options to PayPal controls and Safari toolbar items), and VoiceOver could only reach and read the static time/date text labels; VO+Space on those labels performed no selection. The consequence is that a screen reader or keyboard-only user cannot mark any availability at all, which makes the site's core function unusable nonvisually. The absence of role and name also means that even if focus reached a cell, its purpose and selected/unselected state would not be conveyed.
interventions.mitigation: Make each slot cell a real operable control: either replace the div with a native button or checkbox, or add role="button" (or role="checkbox"/"gridcell" within an appropriate grid structure) plus tabindex so it is reachable by keyboard. Give each cell a programmatic accessible name that combines its column date and row time (for example via aria-label or aria-labelledby pointing at the existing date and time label elements), and expose the selected state programmatically (e.g. aria-pressed or aria-checked) kept in sync with the visual highlight. Bind keydown handlers for Enter and Space to the same selection logic used by the existing pointer handlers, ensure a visible focus indicator is present on the focused cell, and consider arrow-key navigation within the grid so users are not forced to Tab through every slot. If drag-to-select is offered visually, provide an equivalent keyboard path (for example select-start then select-end, or per-cell toggling).

frictions.title: Generic 'Visit linked content' accessible names on carousel cards
frictions.description: VoiceOver announces six interactive carousel cards with identical generic 'Visit linked content' labels, overriding specific image alt text and obscuring card targets (WCAG 2.4.4, 4.1.2).

interventions.description: Update carousel card buttons to use descriptive accessible names based on their contained image alt text.

The homepage gallery/carousel cards are interactive elements whose accessible name is set to the static string 'Visit linked content' (observed on elements matching `.eapp-photo-gallery-item-data-component[aria-label='Visit linked content']`). Where the card already contains an image with meaningful alt text (e.g. 'Little Leaders Characters'), either remove the container-level aria-label so the inner alt text contributes to the name, or compose the label from that text (e.g. 'Visit Little Leaders Characters'). Because the carousel widget may duplicate or re-render slides, apply the naming at the template/data level (or re-apply on slide creation) so cloned slides retain descriptive names rather than reverting to the generic default.

frictions.description: The article's market data charts use generic alt text ('Chart 1' and 'Chart 2'), providing no meaningful summary of visual trends. VoiceOver announces only 'Chart 1, image' and 'Chart 2, image', and drilling in reveals only raw axis numbers without trend descriptions.

interventions.description: Provide descriptive alt text for S&P 500 chart images ('Chart 1' and 'Chart 2') and link them to adjacent explanatory text.

interventions.description: Expose sold-out status on unavailable product size options so screen readers announce availability before selection.

frictions.title: Uber Eats Customization Modal Separates Flavor Labels and Buttons
frictions.description: Under macOS Zoom magnification, flavor labels on the left and '+' increment buttons on the far right of the customization modal cannot fit simultaneously in the viewport, requiring repeated horizontal panning to confirm choices before clicking.

interventions.description: In the item customization modal, each option row places the flavor name at the left edge and the quantity stepper ('-' / count / '+') at the right edge, with a wide empty gap between them. At the magnification level used with macOS Zoom, only one end of a row fits in the visible viewport, so the user repeatedly panned horizontally between the label and the increment button to verify that the quantity being changed belonged to the intended flavor (e.g., setting Lemon Pepper to 5). Consequences: increased interaction cost per selection, loss of the label/control association at high zoom, and a real risk of incrementing the wrong option because the row identity is only conveyed by horizontal alignment that is off-screen when the control is in view.
interventions.mitigation: Reduce the horizontal distance and dependency between an option's label and its stepper control so both remain perceivable together when content is magnified or the viewport is narrow. Concretely: cap the option row's content width (or place the stepper immediately after the label text rather than pinning it to the far right of the modal); allow the row to reflow to a stacked label-above-control layout at narrow effective widths; and ensure each stepper control carries an accessible name that includes the flavor it belongs to (e.g., 'Increase quantity of Lemon Pepper') plus a visible or programmatically associated indication of the current quantity, so the control is self-identifying without needing the distant label in view. Verify the modal at reduced viewport widths / increased zoom levels to confirm no horizontal panning is required to pair a label with its control.

frictions.description: High macOS Zoom magnification prevents viewing complete flight details (times, duration, stops, emissions, price) within a single viewport, forcing continuous horizontal pointer panning across the wide web layout during flight evaluation.

interventions.description: On the flight search results page, all data belonging to one flight option is laid out in a single wide horizontal row, with departure/arrival times at the left edge and price plus the expand control at the right edge. frictions.title: Search results update outside magnified viewport during map navigation
frictions.description: When the user navigates and drags the interactive map under macOS Zoom, the search results panel on the right updates dynamically outside the magnified viewport, forcing the user to pan across the interface to verify updated listings.

interventions.description: Panning/dragging the map updates the search results panel (result count and property cards) at a screen location far from the point of interaction. Under macOS Zoom, the magnified viewport follows the pointer over the map, so the change in the results panel occurs entirely off-screen for the user. The consequence is that the outcome of the user's own action is not perceivable where the action happens: the person must interrupt the task and manually pan across the layout to discover that the visible listing set changed (2,950 -> 31), and risks acting on a stale understanding of the result set in the meantime.
interventions.mitigation: Surface the status of the result-set change near the point of interaction and in a programmatically announced way: expose the updated result count as a live status region (e.g. an ARIA live region / status role updated with text such as '31 results in this map area') so screen readers and other AT announce it without visual scanning, and additionally render a lightweight, dismissible in-map confirmation near the map viewport (for example an overlay chip anchored inside the map container) that reports the new count and links to the results list. Avoid relying solely on a far-off panel repaint to communicate the change, and keep the indicator persistent long enough to be found after panning rather than auto-hiding on a short timer.

frictions.title: Disabled filter controls display active visual styling causing failed clicks
frictions.description: Disabled sidebar filter controls, including checkboxes and filter links, retain active visual styling. When clicked under magnification, they fail to respond and produce a forbidden cursor indicator.

interventions.description: Sidebar filter controls that are unavailable for the current result set (observed with the '$250 - $499.99' price filter checkbox and related filter links) keep the same visual styling as available filters. Under magnification the user targeted and clicked the control twice; instead of applying a filter, the click produced no state change and only a 'forbidden' pointer cursor was shown. Because the disabled state is conveyed only transiently through the cursor and not through the control's own appearance or programmatic state, users spend effort aiming at and clicking targets that cannot act, and receive no persistent explanation of why nothing happened — a cost that is amplified when only a small part of the sidebar is visible in the magnified viewport.
interventions.mitigation: Give unavailable filter controls a distinct, persistent visual treatment (for example reduced emphasis plus explanatory text such as 'no matching results') that does not rely on hover or cursor shape alone, and expose the state programmatically on the control itself (disabled attribute or aria-disabled on the checkbox/link) so the unavailability is available to assistive technology and to users who never see the cursor change. Where a filter is genuinely inapplicable, consider removing it from the list or grouping unavailable filters separately so magnified users do not have to discover it by clicking.

frictions.title: Product listing details exceed magnified viewport requiring repeated horizontal panning
frictions.description: Under screen magnification, product titles and pricing details extend past the viewport width, forcing continuous horizontal panning back and forth across listing cards to read full names and compare specifications.

interventions.description: On the search results page, product card content — full product titles, ratings and pricing — extends beyond the width available in the magnified viewport. The user had to pan horizontally back and forth repeatedly across the single result card to read the complete product name and to correlate it with the price and 'Sold Out' status. Information that belongs to one item is therefore never visible at once, which makes reading and comparison slow and error-prone for magnification users.
interventions.mitigation: Ensure the results layout reflows so listing content wraps within the available width rather than requiring two-dimensional scrolling: allow product titles to wrap over multiple lines instead of extending on a single line, use responsive/fluid card layouts that hold title, rating, price and availability in a single vertically stacked column at narrow effective viewport widths, and verify the search results page at small viewport widths and at large text/zoom levels so no horizontal panning is needed to read a single card.

frictions.title: Navigation menu text low contrast against background slideshow
frictions.description: The main navigation links ('Food & Drinks', 'Menu Guide', etc.) use light cyan text directly overlaid on auto-advancing background photos without a backdrop container, resulting in low visual contrast that makes text difficult to read under magnification.

interventions.description: Apply a dark semi-transparent backdrop behind navigation links to ensure high text contrast over background photos.

On https://fritabatidos.com/ann-arbor/ the main navigation links ('Food & Drinks', 'Menu Guide', etc.) are light cyan text placed directly on top of auto-advancing background photographs, with no opaque or semi-opaque backdrop behind the text. Because the underlying imagery changes continuously and includes light areas, the effective text-to-background contrast is low and unpredictable. The user repeatedly panned and zoomed in and out across the header while the slideshow transitioned, indicating the link labels could not be read reliably even under magnification. Consequence: users cannot dependably identify or distinguish top-level navigation targets, which impedes wayfinding into the rest of the site.
interventions.mitigation: Give the navigation text a guaranteed contrast baseline that does not depend on the current slide: render the nav bar (or each link) on a solid or sufficiently opaque dark backdrop container and pair it with a light text color so the measured contrast ratio meets at least 4.5:1 for the smallest text size used, and verify the ratio against the lightest frame of the slideshow rather than a single representative image. If a transparent header is required for the visual design, add a consistent scrim/overlay layer between the slideshow and the header text, or constrain the slideshow to images pre-processed for a dark upper region. Avoid relying on text-shadow alone as the sole contrast mechanism, and re-check contrast at increased zoom levels where text is scaled but the background continues to change.

interventions.description: The top-navigation mega-menu ('Men', 'Women') is revealed on pointer hover and disappears as soon as the pointer leaves the trigger/panel region. interventions.description: After activating 'Add to Bag' in the product action area, the success confirmation is presented as a mini-cart flyout anchored to the top-right of the page header. Additionally, expose the confirmation programmatically as a status message (e.g., an appropriately scoped live region announcing that the item was added) so the outcome is conveyed without requiring the user to visually locate the header flyout. Avoid relying solely on a fixed-position element in a page corner to communicate the result of an action performed elsewhere on the page.

blind.description: Many primary controls are generic <div>/<span> elements given role="link" or role="button" with tabindex="0" and no href (e.g. the two top-policy items, the cart trigger "Cart", the wish-list entry, the "up to top" and "APP" widgets), so screen-reader users get elements that are announced as links but cannot be reached in the links list or activated with the expected keys.

The search field's visible suggestion text ("bikini", trend icon and label images inside <section aria-hidden="true">) is hidden from assistive technology while it is presented visually and duplicated only as the input placeholder, so screen-reader users are not told what the pre-filled search term is.

The category bar mixes roles incorrectly: a div with role="menubar" contains plain anchors with role="menuitem" and a sibling toggle button ("Categories") that is not part of the menu structure, giving screen-reader users an inaccurate widget model.

Multiple decorative/promotional images are exposed with no accessible name at all (several top-level nodes and the survey/APP overlay images), so screen readers announce unlabeled "image" or file noise instead of skipping or describing them.

Overlay widgets are built as nested interactive elements — a div role="button" named "Sign in" wrapping a real <button> "Sign in", and a div role="button" "Language and Currency Selector" containing a nested role="button" "Choose your language preference" — producing duplicated/confusing focus stops.

The auto-advancing swiper carousels provide only "Previous slide"/"Next slide" buttons (both reported disabled in the accessibility tree for the category carousel) with no live-region or position information, so screen-reader users cannot tell how many slides exist or that content changed.

Product tile links concatenate the whole product name, price and badge into one long accessible name that is visually truncated with an ellipsis (e.g. "6pcs Acrylic Nail Art Brush Set … DIY Nail…"), making listening and comparing items extremely inefficient.

Icon buttons carry information only in an invalid "alt" attribute on a <span> (e.g. alt="sui_icon_policy_shipping_fill_16px") while the SVG is aria-hidden, so no text alternative is actually conveyed for those icons.

low_vision.description: Non-text UI indicators use very light colors against white — the category chevrons are filled rgba(34,34,34,.3) and the search clear icon defaults to #959595 — falling below the 3:1 contrast needed to perceive controls when magnified.

The homepage relies on banner/promo bitmaps (swiper slides, category thumbnails such as "View All", "Bikini Sets" tiles) to present campaign text and prices, so this text pixelates and cannot be resized or re-styled by the user.

The mega-menu is hover/hover-class driven (bs-cate_one-item.hover reveals a very wide multi-column panel) with no mechanism to keep it open or dismiss it, so magnified users lose the panel when the pointer drifts while panning.

Small icon controls such as the 14×14 px nav "Scroll left"/"Scroll right" buttons and the 16 px clear/search icons provide targets well under 24×24 CSS px, which are hard to hit with a magnified, cropped viewport.

The search input has no persistent visible label — its only visible cue is the placeholder "bikini" plus a decorative trend overlay — so once text is entered or the page is magnified, the field's purpose is not visible.

blind.description: In the cookie consent dialog every tab (`#CybotCookiebotDialogNavDeclaration` etc.) is marked `aria-selected="false"` even though the Consent tab carries the `CybotCookiebotDialogActive` class, so screen-reader users are never told which tab/panel is current.

Untranslated template tokens are exposed as accessible names in the consent UI (tab "[#IABV2SETTINGS#]", link "Cross-domain consent[#BULK_CONSENT_DOMAINS_COUNT#]", heading "[#BULK_CONSENT_TITLE#]", text "[#GPC_TOAST_TEXT#]", icon "[#GPC_BANNER_ICON#]"), giving screen-reader users meaningless labels.
All submenu toggle buttons in the header and mobile navigation are announced as "Workspace.Header.ToggleSubmenu" (an untranslated resource key), so blind users cannot tell which menu a button opens.
The consent toggle in the dialog's bottom button wrapper is exposed as `input role="switch"` with no accessible name, so its purpose and state cannot be determined by a screen reader.
The site logo link's accessible name is polluted by inline SVG style text, announcing "Workspace homepage .st0" instead of a clean link name.
The "Mobile menu toggle" control is a plain `<span>` with no role, name-as-button or keyboard affordance, so screen-reader and keyboard users cannot discover or operate the mobile navigation.

The page exposes two level-1 headings with identical text ("Glossary of business terminology" as `<h1>` in the banner and again as a `div role="heading" aria-level="1"`), creating a confusing and duplicated document outline.
Heading levels are inconsistent within the glossary: "PROFIT AND LOSS ACCOUNT" is an `<h3>` while all sibling entries are `<h2>`, breaking the structural pattern used for navigating terms by heading.

The breadcrumb trail is a plain `<ul>` outside any navigation landmark and each link text embeds the separator character ("/Content Hub", "/Business insight"), so the trail is announced with stray slashes and is not identifiable as breadcrumb navigation.
Two different `nav` landmarks share the identical label "Secondary core dropdown links" (desktop and mobile menus) and repeat the same links, so landmark navigation cannot distinguish them.
A hidden reCAPTCHA `textarea` is exposed to the accessibility tree as an unlabeled text box, presenting a control with no name or purpose to screen-reader users.
A tracking pixel image is given meaningful alt text ("dot image pixel") instead of being marked decorative, injecting noise into the screen-reader reading order.
The "Back to top" button's accessible name is duplicated ("Back to top Back to top"), causing redundant announcement.

The consent dialog is rendered as `aria-modal="true"` at the very start of the DOM with `tabindex="-1"` and the underlying page still in the accessibility tree, so screen-reader users can read page content that is visually blocked while no focus containment is provided.

low_vision.description: Consent category state (Necessary/Preferences/Statistics/Marketing) is conveyed only by the position and colour of the custom `CybotCookiebotDialogBodyLevelButtonSlider` graphic with no text on/off indication, which is hard to perceive for users with low vision or colour deficiency.

The cookie dialog content sits inside fixed-height scroll areas (`CybotCookiebotScrollContainer`/`CybotCookiebotScrollArea` with fader overlays), so at high magnification the consent text and buttons are clipped and require nested scrolling.
The page `<h1>` "Glossary of business terminology" is overlaid on a photographic banner `<picture>` image, so the heading text can lack sufficient contrast against the underlying photo.
Literal placeholder strings such as "[#IABV2SETTINGS#]" and "[#GPC_TOAST_TEXT#]" are displayed in the consent dialog, forcing magnified users to interpret broken labels.
The glossary presents over 150 sequential `<h2>` term entries in one long column with no on-page A–Z index or in-page anchors, requiring very extensive scrolling at high magnification.

dhh.description: The primary contact routes surfaced in the header are a telephone number link ("0204 638 0662") and a "Request a callback" button, with no equivalent text-based alternative such as chat offered alongside, disadvantaging users who cannot use voice calls.

friction_results.note: The audit does not report the timer background tab notification issue, focusing instead on contact options.

frictions.title: Small Reddit comment action buttons cause failed pointer activations
frictions.description: The user repeatedly hovers and clicks near small inline comment controls such as Award and Share buttons without successfully activating them, requiring fine pointer corrections on targets below standard target size recommendations.

interventions.description: Enlarge clickable hit areas and padding for Reddit comment action buttons.

On the Reddit comment thread, the inline comment action controls (Award, Share, and vote buttons) present small clickable areas packed closely together in the comment action row. Cursor data over roughly a 16-second window shows repeated fine pointer corrections and four clicks in this region with no resulting activation or view change. The consequence is that users who cannot place the pointer precisely must repeat aim-and-click attempts to reach a control, and mis-aimed clicks may land on adjacent controls or on inert space, making common comment interactions slow and error-prone.
interventions.mitigation: Increase the effective pointer target of each control in the comment action row so that each has a hit area of at least 24x24 CSS pixels (or, if the visible glyph must stay small, provide equivalent spacing so that a 24px circle centred on each target does not overlap the target area of neighbours). This can be done by adding padding or an expanded pseudo-element hit area to the action-row controls (e.g. the award, share, and vote buttons) rather than resizing the icons, keeping the visual layout intact. Verify that the enlarged hit area actually belongs to the interactive element so a click anywhere within it triggers the action.
